Clean a gene list with HGNC

Source: vignettes/articles/hgnc_gene_list.Rmd
hgnc_gene_list.Rmd

The problem

Gene lists arrive from papers, spreadsheets and colleagues with whatever symbols their authors used: aliases (HER2), old symbols (SEPT1), symbols HGNC has withdrawn, and names that are simply not symbols at all. Before such a list can be joined to DrugBank targets, HPO phenotypes or anything else, each entry has to be mapped to an approved HGNC symbol, and the ambiguous ones have to be seen, not guessed.

This article does that with parseHGNC() and dplyr on the HGNC sample that ships with dbparser. It runs offline in a few seconds.

library(dbparser)
library(dplyr)

The list 

genes <- c("PD1", "PDL1", "HER2", "SEPT1", "MARCH1", "FOX1",
           "CBBM", "A12M1", "TP53")

The bundled sample holds only 24 genes and a few withdrawn entries, so every input above was chosen to be in it (or, for FOX1, to show what a miss looks like). On HGNC’s full files the same code covers all approved genes; see Full data below.

Parse the HGNC sample 

hgnc_dir <- system.file("extdata", "hgnc", package = "dbparser")
hgnc <- parseHGNC(file.path(hgnc_dir, "hgnc_complete_set.txt"),
                  withdrawn_path = file.path(hgnc_dir, "withdrawn.txt"))

names(hgnc)
#> [1] "gene"      "gene_name" "withdrawn"
nrow(hgnc$gene)
#> [1] 24

Every dvobject records where its data came from, including the licence and the citation HGNC asks for:

glimpse(get_source_metadata(hgnc))
#> Rows: 1
#> Columns: 12
#> $ metadata_version <chr> "1"
#> $ source           <chr> "hgnc"
#> $ source_name      <chr> "HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (HGNC)"
#> $ release          <chr> NA
#> $ release_date     <date> NA
#> $ retrieved_at     <date> NA
#> $ source_url       <chr> "https://www.genenames.org/download/statistics-and-fi…
#> $ licence          <chr> "CC0-1.0"
#> $ licence_url      <chr> "https://www.genenames.org/about/license/"
#> $ attribution      <chr> "Seal RL, Braschi B, Gray K, McClay J, Tweedie S, Bru…
#> $ files            <list> [<data.frame[2 x 2]>]
#> $ parser           <chr> "dbparser 2.3.0"

HGNC publishes no release number for its current files, so release, release_date and retrieved_at are NA here; pass them to parseHGNC() when you parse your own download.

Match each input

gene_name has one row per approved symbol, alias and previous symbol (and the names, which we do not need here). Each row carries its gene’s hgnc_id, so a match gives the approved symbol directly.

approved <- hgnc$gene |>
  select(hgnc_id, matched = symbol)

name_hits <- hgnc$gene_name |>
  filter(kind %in% c("symbol", "alias_symbol", "prev_symbol")) |>
  inner_join(approved, by = "hgnc_id") |>
  transmute(input = name,
            matched,
            how = recode(kind,
                         symbol       = "approved",
                         alias_symbol = "alias",
                         prev_symbol  = "previous"))

Withdrawn symbols are in their own table, with the gene or genes HGNC merged or split them into. An entry withdrawn outright points nowhere.

withdrawn_hits <- hgnc$withdrawn |>
  transmute(input   = withdrawn_symbol,
            matched = merged_into_symbol,
            how     = "withdrawn")

Join the list to both, keeping every match: an input that fits several genes gets several rows here.

hits <- tibble(input = genes) |>
  left_join(bind_rows(name_hits, withdrawn_hits),
            by = "input", relationship = "one-to-many") |>
  distinct()

hits
#> # A tibble: 14 × 3
#>    input  matched how      
#>    <chr>  <chr>   <chr>    
#>  1 PD1    PDCD1   alias    
#>  2 PD1    SNCA    alias    
#>  3 PD1    SPATA2  alias    
#>  4 PDL1   CD274   alias    
#>  5 HER2   ERBB2   alias    
#>  6 SEPT1  SEPTIN1 previous 
#>  7 MARCH1 MARCHF1 previous 
#>  8 FOX1   NA      NA       
#>  9 CBBM   OPN1LW  previous 
#> 10 CBBM   OPN1MW  previous 
#> 11 CBBM   OPN1MW  withdrawn
#> 12 CBBM   OPN1LW  withdrawn
#> 13 A12M1  NA      withdrawn
#> 14 TP53   TP53    approved

One row per input

Collapse to one row per input. needs_choice is TRUE when an input fits more than one approved gene; these are listed, not resolved.

clean <- hits |>
  group_by(input) |>
  summarise(
    needs_choice = n_distinct(na.omit(matched)) > 1,
    how          = if (all(is.na(how))) "no match"
                   else paste(unique(na.omit(how)), collapse = ", "),
    matched      = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(matched))), collapse = ", "),
    .groups      = "drop") |>
  select(input, matched, how, needs_choice) |>
  arrange(match(input, genes))

knitr::kable(clean)
input matched how needs_choice
PD1 PDCD1, SNCA, SPATA2 alias TRUE
PDL1 CD274 alias FALSE
HER2 ERBB2 alias FALSE
SEPT1 SEPTIN1 previous FALSE
MARCH1 MARCHF1 previous FALSE
FOX1 no match FALSE
CBBM OPN1LW, OPN1MW previous, withdrawn TRUE
A12M1 withdrawn FALSE
TP53 TP53 approved FALSE

What the table shows:

  • TP53 is an approved symbol; nothing to do.
  • HER2 and PDL1 are aliases of ERBB2 and CD274.
  • SEPT1 and MARCH1 are previous symbols: HGNC renamed them SEPTIN1 and MARCHF1. The gene table has the date of each change.
  • PD1 is an alias of three genes (PDCD1, SNCA and SPATA2). Most readers mean PDCD1, but the list does not say so, and only its author can.
  • CBBM is a previous symbol of both OPN1LW and OPN1MW, and HGNC’s withdrawn file records it as split into the same two genes, so it needs a choice too.
  • A12M1 was withdrawn and points to no gene.
  • FOX1 finds nothing. In this sample RBFOX1 has the alias FOX-1, with a hyphen; exact matching does not guess that the two are the same.
hgnc$gene |>
  filter(symbol %in% c("SEPTIN1", "MARCHF1")) |>
  select(symbol, prev_symbol, date_symbol_changed)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   symbol  prev_symbol date_symbol_changed
#>   <chr>   <chr>       <date>             
#> 1 MARCHF1 MARCH1      2019-07-09         
#> 2 SEPTIN1 DIFF6|SEPT1 2019-04-04

Withdrawn symbols

The withdrawn table keeps HGNC’s own status for the withdrawn ID and for each gene it points to:

hgnc$withdrawn |>
  filter(withdrawn_symbol %in% genes) |>
  select(withdrawn_symbol, status, merged_into_symbol, merged_into_status)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   withdrawn_symbol status          merged_into_symbol merged_into_status
#>   <chr>            <chr>           <chr>              <chr>             
#> 1 A12M1            Entry Withdrawn NA                 NA                
#> 2 CBBM             Merged/Split    OPN1MW             Approved          
#> 3 CBBM             Merged/Split    OPN1LW             Approved

Next steps

Inputs with needs_choice = TRUE, a withdrawn match with no target, or no match at all go back to whoever wrote the list. The rest map one-to-one to an approved symbol and can be joined to other sources, for example DrugBank targets or HPO gene-phenotype associations.

Full data

The sample is enough to show the method, not to clean a real list. The script announce/hgnc_full.R in the package repository runs the same steps on your own download of hgnc_complete_set.txt and withdrawn.txt from genenames.org.
